verification: Linked original texts were opened and relevant passages inspected. NBER pages returned 403; the author-hosted published paper and survey authors official Fed article were used instead. This is a focused evidence packet, not an exhaustive latest-market review.

sources.title: Generative AI at Work
sources.authors: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, Lindsey Raymond
sources.type: Peer-reviewed empirical study; author-hosted published text
sources.finding: Among 5,172 support agents at one business-software firm, AI assistance increased issues resolved per hour by 15% on average; effects differed by experience and skill. Highly skilled workers had small quality declines.
sources.supports: A plausible benefit hypothesis for assisted customer service and a reason to evaluate quality alongside speed.
sources.limitations: One firm and an earlier system; not an e-commerce trial, a current-model benchmark, or a guarantee of cost savings. Use the published version consistently, not the earlier 14% working-paper estimate.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
sources.locator: Introduction; risk overview, sections on confabulation, data privacy and human-AI configuration
sources.finding: Identifies false output, privacy disclosure, and human overreliance as generative-AI risks; advocates context-sensitive risk management.
sources.supports: Evaluate correctness, data exposure and review effectiveness before expansion. Human approval alone is not assurance.
sources.limitations: Not binding law, a certification, a measured failure rate, or evidence that either hypothetical organization has effective controls.

sources.title: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes
sources.locator: Test and evaluate; Security and privacy considerations; Known limitations
sources.finding: RAG retrieves source content to ground responses. Quality depends on preparation and retrieval; inaccurate answers and sensitive-data leakage remain possible.
sources.supports: Audit knowledge quality and retrieval, validate answers and access controls; weak knowledge maintenance is a relevant organizational constraint.
sources.limitations: Vendor guidance, not independent effectiveness evidence; not a recommendation to buy Azure or proof that RAG eliminates errors.

sources.title: The State of Generative AI Adoption in 2025
sources.authors: Alexander Bick, Adam Blandin, David Deming
sources.locator: Generative AI Adoption Continues to Climb
sources.type: Original survey authors reporting results at the St. Louis Fed
sources.finding: Reports 54.6% overall generative-AI usage and 37.4% work usage in August 2025 among the relevant US working-age survey population; earlier estimates were reweighted after question-sequencing changes.
sources.limitations: Self-reported individual usage, not e-commerce enterprise deployment or success. Not a November 2026 adoption estimate; does not establish technical maturity or return on investment.

analyst_inferences: Potential productivity benefits justify evaluation, not guaranteed implementation.
Different knowledge maintenance and approvals can change management action while technology evidence remains constant.

Proposed pilot metrics: factual/policy correctness, unsupported claims, privacy incidents, reviewer effort and total handling time versus the existing workflow. These are proposed evaluation choices, not observed results or thresholds mandated by sources.
remaining_gaps: No measured company baseline or test outcomes.
No verified vendor, integration, pricing, data-processing terms or jurisdiction-specific requirements.
No directly comparable e-commerce production adoption rate.
No specific current model assessed; no global maturity rating justified.
usage_instruction: Provide this identical packet with both prompt packets. Keep findings separate from hypothetical case assumptions. A local file path alone does not supply its content to ChatGPT; include the contents explicitly when running the tests.
